# Installed OpenAI SDK protocol fixture

This optional offline test uses the actual OpenAI Python SDK **2.54.0**, HTTPX **0.28.1** and the seventeen exact wheels recorded in `requirements.lock` and `selected-wheels.json`. It runs on standalone Python **3.12**, which matches the compiled wheels. It does not install or execute full Hermes, whose pinned runtime requires Python 3.14. No dependency is silently substituted.

`decision-hermes-installed-sdk.test.ts` executes the existing pinned Hermes kwargs builder, then passes its captured original kwargs and explicitly declared caller streaming flags to the installed SDK. SDK-only timeout handling, JSON serialization, HTTP header construction, JSON/SSE parsing and streamed tool-call assembly are performed by the real SDK. Actual SDK-assembled message objects enter the previously pinned original assistant/result constructors with their disclosed synthetic agent collaborators. Synthetic results are supplied; no tools run.

HTTPX uses `MockTransport` with `trust_env=False`; OpenAI uses a synthetic key/base URL and `max_retries=0`. Python socket creation/DNS is rejected. The transport exchanges bounded JSONL messages over child stdio with the Node fixture: SDK request bytes enter the actual authenticated application POST handler, and its response headers/chunks return to the SDK on demand. There is no loopback HTTP server or alternate gateway. The closed fetch allowlist contains three exact URL constants: the mock Zen selector, mock Claude executor and mock AGY executor; the AGY URL is enabled only in AGY fixture mode. Unexpected dispatches are counted cumulatively and fail the suite.

The fixture limits each line, request body, response chunk, total response and number of SDK requests. Cancellation closes the actual application response reader. A child deadline fails the test; a killed or nonzero process is never counted as a successful SDK run. Logs and result assertions contain synthetic data only. The private installation log and machine-specific venv are not repository deliverables.

Configure an isolated exact venv outside the repository, using normal TLS verification and the official hash-locked wheel URLs. For this recorded run the venv is `/tmp/native-hermes-sdk-20261026/venv`; it is not a portable shipped runtime. Set `OMNIROUTE_HERMES_SDK_PYTHON` to its Python executable when running the test. Without an explicit executable the test is visibly skipped, not SDK evidence. With one provided, missing packages or version mismatches fail rather than falling back to global packages.

The package lock is for reproducible dependency installation only. It is not permission to make provider calls or use real credentials. Run the application test with the repository's offline network guard and isolated per-process DATA_DIR. Passing demonstrates the tested SDK serialization/parsing and guarded synthetic application path, not full Hermes runtime compatibility, real provider signature acceptance, account entitlement, selection quality or deployment readiness.

The strengthened fixture uses the same approved synthetic source base, `https://hermes.fixture.invalid/v1`, and forwards every SDK-generated request header. It maps the `/v1/chat/completions` path explicitly to the existing `/api/v1/chat/completions` POST function; it does not claim TCP/TLS or full Next.js-server coverage. Python socket/DNS guards are installed after the verified SDK imports and before client construction; the claim is no provider sockets during the tested fixture, not a general import-time syscall sandbox.

The five additional opt-in effort-profile cases consume the separately reviewed `hermesEffort` fixture. They prove that omitted effort stays absent through both SDK tool-loop requests while the router selects and pins an allowed pair, that explicit Medium/High remain explicit, and that explicit/recovery Off are not silently changed into enabled thinking. The configured synthetic execution pool cannot honor Off, so those two cases must reject before any decision or execution. The optional relay profile and its narrow guards are source fixtures reviewed separately; they do not change ordinary Hermes defaults or prove a full installed Hermes runtime.

Tool-result construction now uses the two exact pinned Hermes split/derive ID helper bodies rather than the legacy fixture-ID prefix facades. Gateway correlation IDs pass through the real SDK and original constructors unchanged; native ID absence is handled separately by the guarded provider adapter. Those pure helper bodies are source/AST and hash checked, and their unused random fallback is denied. Remaining declared collaborators, standalone Python 3.12, two-request fixture bound and full-Hermes/runtime limits still apply.

## Explicit configured-control cases

Five named `hermesPinned` cases supply synthetic configured inputs to the unchanged original `_build_chat_completions_kwargs` and profile transport. `temperature: 0.7` and `top_p: 0.9` come from the original `request_overrides` merge; they are test values, not Hermes defaults. Strict absent/false/true come from supplied tool declarations, with the same valid item schema in all five cases. The fixture does not execute the full registry, CLI configuration or plugin loader. Recognizing `top_p` in the fixture's explicit projection allowlist reflects a field the original profile code already forwards; it changes no pinned source fragment or router eligibility.

Ten SDK cases check both captured kwargs and actual SDK request bytes before the real handler outcome. They use the same High, cap, stream and declaration shape, with these current contracts:

| Configured input   | Claude                                                    | AGY                                               |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `temperature: 0.7` | Unsupported: handler 409, zero decision/execution         | Same                                              |
| `top_p: 0.9`       | Unsupported: handler 409, zero decision/execution         | Same                                              |
| `strict` absent    | Allowed; native strict flag omitted                       | Allowed                                           |
| `strict: false`    | False preserved on client wire; native non-strict default | Unsupported: handler 409, zero decision/execution |
| `strict: true`     | True preserved on client wire and native tool             | Unsupported: handler 409, zero decision/execution |

Allowed Claude cases retain two eligible Claude choices and use one decision plus one execution. The isolated AGY controls use a sole AGY candidate, so valid absence uses zero decisions and one execution; a supported Claude alternate cannot hide an AGY rejection. Unsupported cases must reach the actual handler after SDK serialization and create no provider-attempt journal records. Empty journals are not treated as reported zero-cost usage. The fixtures do not claim live provider acceptance, honored Gemini sampling, structured-output quality or full Hermes compatibility.
